title: Notes for a Community Exhibition
paragraphs: The community center was planning an exhibition about everyday experiences. Students volunteered to select the written material. Their challenge was to find a balance between vivid individual moments and a larger theme that visitors could follow without already knowing the people involved.

The opening pages introduced several situations worth examining carefully. During the emergency, our neighboring town became a valuable ally. Her distant ancestor arrived in the valley two hundred years ago. The captain has authority to order the ship back to port. An anonymous benefactor donated enough money to rebuild the library.

The remaining pages widened the discussion with additional observations. As a citizen of the country, she could vote in its elections. My father's colleague works with him in the same laboratory. The whole community gathered to celebrate the town's anniversary. Her trusted companion joined her on the long journey.

By the end of the discussion, the students had learned why careful reading requires more than a quick judgment. A useful interpretation must fit the details of the situation. They chose a conclusion that acknowledged differences among the accounts, and they left readers with a question: which observation most strongly supports your view, and what might change your mind?

targets.definition: a person or group providing support
a person from an earlier family generation
the power to make and enforce decisions
someone who gives help or money
a legally recognized member of a country
a group linked by place or shared interests
